key_insight: The paper argues that current world models can generate convincing observations, but they often lack a persistent internal state that continues evolving when the scene is unobserved. In short: they can render the world, but they do not yet truly remember or maintain the world.
problem_solved: It addresses the gap in evaluation benchmarks that measure frame quality or short-term prediction, but fail to test whether a model preserves object permanence, long-range continuity, and state evolution independent of observation.
method: Reframes world-model evaluation around persistent internal state rather than only visual reconstruction quality.
Highlights benchmark blind spots that let models appear competent without maintaining a coherent hidden world state over time.
Motivates evaluation tasks where entities must remain consistent and events must progress even when not directly observed.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this means better benchmarks are needed before world models can be trusted for planning, simulation, and embodied agents. Models that pass visual tests may still fail in real-world settings if they cannot retain a stable latent state across time.

paper_title: Current World Models Lack a Persistent State Core
paper_authors: Jinpeng Lu, Dexu Zhu, Haoyuan Shi, Linghan Cai, Guo Tang
